title: Anonymous Group Signatures for Distributed Systems
key_claim: Group signatures provide signer anonymity while allowing an authorised opener to reveal the signer.

title: Lattice-Based Anonymous Signatures
key_claim: Lattice constructions can provide post-quantum anonymity and traceability.

title: Distributed Opening for Post-Quantum Group Signatures
key_claim: Traceability can be implemented using distributed threshold opening rather than one trusted opener.

title: INW: Independent NeRF Watermarking Architecture Toward Efficient and Robust Copyright Protection
topic: Copyright protection of Neural Radiance Fields via model watermarking
method: Trains a NeRF, prunes Least Significant Neurons by weight L2 norm, records their positions as a binary secret key, then retrains only the masked LSN subnetwork to encode an implicit watermark NeRF that the key holder can extract
key_claim: Exploiting parameter redundancy lets a watermark be embedded into a pre-trained NeRF without the creator taking part, with 100% lossless watermark extraction and rendering quality comparable to an unwatermarked NeRF (PSNR 31.73).
limitation: The watermark is effectively erased by random structured pruning above a 20% ratio, the secret key must be transmitted alongside the model, and evaluation uses only the synthetic Blender dataset.

title: MBRS: Enhancing Robustness of DNN-based Watermarking by Mini-Batch of Real and Simulated JPEG Compression
topic: Robust deep-learning image watermarking against JPEG compression
method: Encoder-noise-decoder network that randomly picks real JPEG, differentiable simulated JPEG-Mask or identity as the noise layer for each mini-batch, with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks, a message processor, a strength factor and an optional diffusion block for crop robustness
key_claim: Mixing real and simulated JPEG across mini-batches achieves a bit error rate below 0.01% under JPEG Q=50 while keeping encoded-image PSNR above 36 dB.
limitation: The base model is vulnerable to crop and cropout, and the diffusion block that fixes this requires a shorter 30-bit message while crop error remains around 4%.

title: TrustMark: Universal Watermarking for Arbitrary Resolution Images
topic: Imperceptible robust image watermarking for content provenance and C2PA
method: GAN-trained MUNIT-based embedder with 1x1-convolution post-processing and focal frequency loss, ResNet50 extractor, 18 differentiable noise transforms, residual-interpolation resolution scaling, and a KBNet-based watermark remover (TrustMark-RM) for re-watermarking
key_claim: TrustMark achieves state-of-the-art imperceptibility (PSNR above 40 dB) and robustness across CLIC, DIV2K and MetFace at arbitrary resolution, and imperceptible watermarks can be removed with a denoising network for re-watermarking.
limitation: Highly cluttered images yield lower PSNR and bit accuracy, and the denoising benefit of TrustMark-RM weakens as noise accumulates over repeated re-watermarking.

title: Video Seal: Open and Efficient Video Watermarking
topic: Open-source neural video watermarking robust to codecs and editing
method: U-Net embedder and ViT-Small extractor embedding 96 bits, temporal watermark propagation every k=4 frames with downscale/upscale inference, multistage training (image pre-training, hybrid image-video training with straight-through H.264, extractor fine-tuning)
key_claim: Video Seal is more robust than HiDDeN, MBRS, CIN, TrustMark and WAM, especially under combined geometric transformations and video compression, while remaining efficient and imperceptible.
limitation: As a post-hoc method it is less secure than generation-time watermarking, it hides fewer bits than MBRS or TrustMark, and temporal propagation can introduce visible shadow artifacts in fast-moving video.

title: FiLM-CAM: Keyed Feature Modulation for Conditional-Access Watermarking
topic: Conditional-access image watermarking where embedding, decoding and removal require a secret key
method: A 100-bit binary key is mapped by an MLP to a 64-d embedding that produces FiLM scale and shift parameters modulating the U-Net embedder bottleneck and the ConvNeXt-Base extractor head; watermarks are composed in tanh logit space with an image-dependent gain, trained with correct-key and wrong-key (all-zero target) steps, and removed by re-running the embedder and inverting the composition with 20 iterative refinement steps
key_claim: Keyed FiLM modulation gives a single shared watermarking backbone conditional access, with about 0.99 bit accuracy and about 46 dB PSNR under the correct key, near-chance (0.53-0.55) decoding under wrong keys, and key-gated removal reaching about 54-58 dB PSNR.
limitation: Access control is learned rather than cryptographic, and wrong-key removal still partly strips the watermark (post-removal bit accuracy about 0.78-0.81 rather than full recovery), with removal generalising across keys if the remover is trained without the noise layer.
